metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ranchettes, WY
metaDescription: Own minerals near Ranchettes outside Cheyenne, on the Wyoming reach of the DJ Basin? We check the actual title before quoting a number.
heroLead: Ranchettes is a small residential community just outside Cheyenne, on subdivided acreage that was farm and ranch ground within recent memory.
intro: As Cheyenne has grown outward, former agricultural land in Laramie County has been split into small acreages like Ranchettes, and the mineral rights under those lots do not always follow the surface. Laramie County sits at the northern edge of the DJ Basin, so a mineral interest here can carry real activity depending on exactly where your tract falls.

The name itself gives away the area's history — small ranchette parcels carved out of larger agricultural tracts as Cheyenne's population grew, with mineral rights sometimes staying whole under multiple lots rather than splitting with each sale.

sections.heading: Small-acreage split estate
paragraphs: When agricultural ground gets subdivided into small residential lots, mineral rights are commonly reserved by the seller or an earlier owner rather than transferred with the surface. If you own a home site in Ranchettes, that does not automatically mean you own the minerals beneath it, and it is worth confirming through the deed record before assuming either way.

sections.heading: DJ Basin proximity
paragraphs: Laramie County's position at the edge of the DJ Basin means leasing and drilling interest has ebbed and flowed here depending on commodity prices and how operators are focusing their Colorado-adjacent programs. We check current activity specific to your legal description rather than assuming based on the general area.

sections.heading: What to send us
paragraphs: A division order, check stub, or old deed with your legal description is what we need to start tracing your interest and putting together an offer.

faqs.question: I own a lot in Ranchettes — do the minerals come with it?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Subdivided acreage frequently has minerals reserved separately. We confirm that through Laramie County deed records.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Ranchettes?
faqs.answer: It varies by specific tract and time period. We check current Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission filings before making an offer.

faqs.question: What if I inherited a mineral fraction and don't have any paperwork?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever you have, even a name and rough location, and we'll work to trace it through county records.

faqs.question: If my lot is small, does that mean my mineral interest is small too?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. A mineral interest under a subdivided ranchette lot can still tie back to a larger original tract, so lot size and mineral share aren't always proportional.
